craft_claim: A resilient dramatic premise requires a dynamic, dialectical clash between mutually exclusive values rather than a static situation.

supporting_evidence.note: Egri defines premise as proposition containing three parts: character, conflict, and conclusion (e.g. 'Ruthless ambition leads to destruction').
Dialectic between relentless pursuit of civic truth and catastrophic personal guilt drives all dramatic action.

counterevidence.note: Modernist interior narratives may replace dialectical collision with atmospheric psychological association.

scope: Applies universally across classical, dramatic, and narrative fiction where causal progression drives reader engagement.
exceptions: Lyrical vignettes and purely associative modernist or stream-of-consciousness narratives.
